title: Linux ALSA, Pipewire, no MIDI devices connected OS.get_connected_midi_inputs
body:
### Tested versions

Godot v4.5.1.stable.arch_linux

on my system, ArchLinux ALSA, Pipewire, no MIDI devices connected OS.get_connected_midi_inputs.

`func _ready():
	print("opening midi inputs..")
	OS.open_midi_inputs()
	print("available midi inputs: ")
	print(OS.get_connected_midi_inputs())`

Prints empty [] input list, same issue if I loop on process() for get_connected_midi_inputs()

running with --verbose the only useful output I get that's audio related is below. Nothing MIDI related.. I am not seeing much interesting show up in Raysession (my pipewire client). Whereas other applications do just fine. Firefox works fine, and detects my midi devices there. An electron JS app does, as well (a desktop app, not in browser)

PulseAudio 17.0.0 detected.
PulseAudio: context other
PulseAudio: context other
PulseAudio: context other
PulseAudio: context ready
PulseAudio: Detecting channels for device: alsa_output.pci-0000_0d_00.1.hdmi-stereo-extra3
PulseAudio: detected 2 output channels
PulseAudio: audio buffer frames: 512 calculated output latency: 11ms


in some digging I did, I found https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/69151 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5881 . Don't know how these relate and if these still apply or would fix my issue. Not sure their status yet.

### System information

Linux ArchLinux KDE ALSA PulseAudio Pipewire Godot v4.5.1.stable.arch_linux

### Issue description

 no MIDI devices shown as connected when calling OS.get_connected_midi_inputs.

### Steps to reproduce

Run above sample code, Linux, archlinux, pipewire, with Godot 4 version above. No devices will show up or therefore be able to be used...

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

In any simple GDscript file/project, this should return something non-null.

`func _ready():
	print("opening midi inputs..")
	OS.open_midi_inputs()
	print("available midi inputs: ")
	print(OS.get_connected_midi_inputs())`
